title: Ops signal playbook and OKR sandbox — Q1 2026
content:
Purpose: quick, tactical working doc to converge on the company-level OKR candidates for Q1 2026 and a pragmatic ops playbook for surfacing and resolving "signals" that matter for customers and platform reliability. This is intentionally noisy — call-out the TODOs, edit the KR targets, and add concrete owners.

Executive summary (1 paragraph):
- Problem: As usage continues to scale across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments, product incidents and pricing/latency regressions are the primary friction points for logo expansion and renewals. We need a small set of company-level commitments (OKRs) that align engineering, product, SRE, and CS on measurable outcomes, plus an operational signal-playbook to make diagnosis and escalation fast and consistent.
- Proposal: 3 company OKRs (Reliability, Cost/unit, Time-to-value) + a 1-page Ops Signal Playbook (triage steps, owner matrix, surfaced dashboards), packaged in the Q1 all-hands to create focus and measurable follow-through.

Draft company-level OKRs (candidate list — pick 1–3):
OKR 1: Reliability & graceful degradation
- Objective: Reduce customer-facing severity-1 incidents and improve graceful degradation surfaces.
- KR1.1: Decrease P1 incident rate affecting customer traffic by 45% quarter-over-quarter (baseline: Jan 2026).
- KR1.2: Deploy model fallback policy across top 10 customers (by revenue) and verify availability >99.5% during simulated cluster outages.
- KR1.3: Reduce mean time to mitigation (first mitigation action after alert) from 12 minutes to under 6 minutes.

OKR 2: Unit economics edge (cost per token/embedding)
- Objective: Improve inference economics without reducing output quality.
- KR2.1: Reduce average token cost for mid-sequence requests (20–512 tokens) by 18% through batching, cache, and runtime kernel tuning.
- KR2.2: Ship Optimize recommendations engine MVP and get 60% adoption on eligible routes for early customers (>=3 customers).
- KR2.3: Show no more than 2% measured quality regression on canonical eval set for routes that enable aggressive quantization profiles.

OKR 3: Time-to-value for new customers
- Objective: Shorten the onboarding funnel and time from sign-up to production traffic.
- KR3.1: Decrease median time from signup to first production request to <48 hours for self-serve customers.
- KR3.2: Create and ship 3 reference templates (chat, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings similarity) with one-click deploy for Dedicated.
- KR3.3: Increase NPS from 7 -> 8.2 on onboarding surveys for customers that used a reference template.

Notes on selection: pick max 2 objectives for company-level focus this quarter. My recommendation: O1 (Reliability) + O2 (Unit economics). O3 is high-value but many teams are already owning smaller growth goals — keep it as a program-level OKR.

All-hands framing (how we present it):
- 10 minute opener from CEO (context: why these OKRs matter for customers and scaling economics).
- 15 minute product ops demo: show the Ops Signal Playbook in action (a simulated incident + escalation + mitigation + follow-up).
- 10 minute lightning wins: 3 stories showing improvements in latency/cost/uptime from teams.
- 15 minute breakout: cross-functional groups pick the top 2 execution risks and propose mitigations (report back).
- Deliverable: public one-pager with final company OKRs and a sign-up sheet (owners + liaisons) within 48 hours after the all-hands.

Ops Signal Playbook (working checklist — keep short):
1) Signal definition & priority
- Signal types: latency anomaly (95th/99th), token-cost spike, model-quality drift (eval drop), error-rate increase, billing/usage anomaly.
- Priority classification: S1 (customer impact on prod traffic), S2 (degrades performance but fallback exists), S3 (investigate, no immediate customer impact).

2) Detection & routing
- Primary monitors: per-customer latency dashboard, route-level cost per 1k tokens, model-variant quality SLO dashboard, billing delta monitor.
- Routing: alerts go to #ops-signals Slack channel via PagerDuty for S1; S2 -> #platform-warn; S3 -> internal ticketing queue.
- Quick filters: tag by affected product (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and by customer tier (self-serve / enterprise).

3) Triage (first 10 minutes)
- Actor: whoever picks the PDB (on-call SRE or platform eng) posts initial assessment with one-line hypothesis and immediate mitigation (fallback, scale up, rate-limiting) in #ops-signals.
- Immediate actions: apply model fallback if quality tolerable, scale Dedicated pool, or enable burst reserve. If billing spike, throttle non-critical routes.

4) Escalation & communication
- Escalate to incident lead (rotating list) if not mitigated in 12 minutes for S1.
- Customer comms: Customer Success drafts an initial note (templated) for affected customers, set to "We are investigating; mitigation applied".
- Postmortem owner assigned within 24 hours.

5) Post-incident
- Postmortem triage in 72 hours: severity, root cause, follow-up actions, and tracked KRs impacted.
- Add signal to long-term metric dashboard and watchlist if it recurs.

Owner matrix (proposal):
- Detection & instrumentation: observability + platform-engineering (Clara Ruiz)
- Triage & immediate mitigation: SRE + serving-runtime (Jonah Reed)
- Customer comms: customer-success (Priya Singh)
- OKR tracking & coordination: product-ops (Maya Thompson)
- Runbook maintenance: console-and-tooling docs team

Immediate execution plan (next 4 weeks):
Week 0 (this doc): agree on final company OKRs, owners, and all-hands agenda.
Week 1: finalize 1-page playbook, create Slack templates and PagerDuty routing, instrument missing metrics for top 25 routes.
Week 2: tabletop incident at all-hands rehearsal, validate fallbacks for top-5 enterprise customers (dry run).
Week 3: ship Optimize recommendations engine toggles for internal beta, roll out batching/caching quick wins to 3 high-traffic routes.
Week 4: consolidate KR baselines and publish company-facing one-pager + sign-up.

Key risks & mitigations (open list):
- Risk: quantization changes cause unseen quality regressions. Mitigation: gated rollout + eval harness + holdback cohort.
- Risk: Dedicated autoscale limits lead to late mitigations. Mitigation: introduce emergency burst policy and test failovers weekly.
- Risk: CS bandwidth to field customer comms during incidents. Mitigation: pre-authorized templates + shifts for enterprise owners.

Open questions (please edit inline):
- Which two KRs do we lock for the company level? (Reliability vs Unit economics vs Time-to-value)
- Do we require product teams to reserve a 10% Q1 capacity budget for incident dry runs?
- Who will own the final OKR doc and quarterly cadence for reviews? (Recommend: product-ops + head of eng as co-chairs)

- [ ] Jonah: schedule dry-run for model fallback with top-5 enterprise customers (due Mar 12).

Notes to reviewers: This doc is intentionally compact — pick the two company-level OKRs and focus on embedding the ops playbook as a repeatable social contract across product, SRE, and CS. Add comments where the KRs or deadlines feel unrealistic. The all-hands slot is intentionally a rehearsal setting — the goal is to leave with owners and a checklist.
